errors.title: Operand size mismatch
causes: Mixing an 8-bit operand with a 16-bit operand, e.g. MOV AL, BX.
Moving a word variable (DW) into an 8-bit register, or a byte variable (DB) into a 16-bit register.
fixes: Use registers of the same size (AL with BL, AX with BX).
Match the variable type: DB with 8-bit registers, DW with 16-bit registers.
Use BYTE PTR or WORD PTR when the size cannot be known, e.g. MOV BYTE PTR [SI], 05h.

errors.title: Undefined symbol
causes: A label or variable is misspelled or not declared.
A hex number starts with a letter (FFh) so it is read as a symbol name.
fixes: Check the spelling of labels and variables.
Add a leading 0 to hex numbers that start with A-F (write 0FFh).

errors.pattern: immediate mode illegal|illegal immediate|improper operand type|invalid use of register
errors.title: Illegal immediate operand
causes: Moving an immediate value directly into a segment register (MOV DS, 1000h or MOV DS, @DATA).
Using an immediate with MUL or DIV (MUL 05h).
fixes: Load the value into AX first, then MOV DS, AX.
Load the operand into a register first, then MUL/DIV that register.

errors.title: Invalid operand combination
causes: Memory-to-memory operation such as MOV VAR1, VAR2.
Unsupported operand for the instruction (e.g. OUT 0FFE6h, AL with a port above FFh).
Segment register to segment register move (MOV ES, DS).
fixes: Move through a register: MOV AL, VAR2 then MOV VAR1, AL.
For ports above FFh load the address into DX and use OUT DX, AL.
Copy segment registers through a general register: MOV AX, DS then MOV ES, AX.

errors.title: Divide error / divide overflow
causes: The divisor is zero.
The quotient is too large for AL (8-bit DIV) or AX (16-bit DIV).
DX was not cleared before a 16-bit DIV, so DX:AX is a huge number.
fixes: Check that the divisor is not 0.
Use a 16-bit divisor if the quotient does not fit in 8 bits.
Add XOR DX, DX (or MOV DX, 0) before a 16-bit DIV.

errors.title: Illegal instruction or syntax error
causes: Typing mistake in an instruction (MOVE instead of MOV).
Using a 80386+ instruction or register (EAX, MOVZX) in an 8086 program.
Missing comma between operands.
fixes: Check the spelling of the instruction on the reported line.
Use only 8086 instructions and 16-bit registers.
Write operands as DEST, SOURCE separated by a comma.

errors.pattern: missing (or unreachable )?cs|no stack|end of file|missing end|unexpected end|open procedure|unclosed
errors.title: Missing END / segment / procedure closure
causes: The program does not finish with END MAIN.
A PROC has no matching ENDP.
The .STACK directive or segment ASSUME is missing (warning in LINK).
fixes: End the program with MAIN ENDP and END MAIN.
Add .STACK 100h after .MODEL SMALL.

errors.pattern: jump (out of range|destination too far)|relative jump out of range|short jump
errors.title: Jump out of range
causes: Conditional jumps on the 8086 can only reach -128 to +127 bytes.
fixes: Reverse the condition and jump over a JMP: replace JE FAR_LABEL with JNE SKIP / JMP FAR_LABEL / SKIP:.

errors.title: Program does not terminate / infinite loop
causes: CX is 0 when LOOP starts (LOOP then runs 65536 times) or CX is changed inside the loop.
No exit instruction (MOV AH,4Ch / INT 21h or HLT).
The loop label is placed before the counter initialisation.
fixes: Load CX with the count before the loop and do not modify CX inside it (or PUSH/POP it).
End the program with MOV AH, 4Ch and INT 21h (DOS) or HLT (kit).
Place the label after the initialisation instructions.

errors.title: Wrong or unexpected output
causes: DS not initialised, so variables are read from the wrong segment.
Bytes read in reverse order (little-endian).
Signed jumps used for unsigned data, or vice versa.
Values entered in decimal instead of hex (missing 'h').
fixes: Add MOV AX, @DATA / MOV DS, AX at the start.
Remember that memory stores the low byte first: 68ACh appears as AC 68.
Use JA/JB/JAE/JBE for unsigned data and JG/JL/JGE/JLE for signed data.
Add the 'h' suffix to every hex number.

errors.pattern: dosbox|not recognized as an internal|command not found|masm.exe|tasm.exe|cannot find
errors.title: Assembler or tool not found
causes: MASM/TASM folder not mounted in DOSBox.
Running MASM in a modern Windows terminal, which cannot run 16-bit programs.
fixes: In DOSBox: MOUNT C C:\8086 then C: and run MASM from that folder.
Use DOSBox or emu8086 — 64-bit Windows cannot run 16-bit DOS programs directly.
